title: Islands worth the time
standfirst: Thousands of islands, of which perhaps six are worth a member's fortnight in any given season.

blocks.heading: A boat as the hotel
paras: The archipelago is too large to travel by hotel. Beyond Bali, the good way to move is on a boat that sleeps you between islands.
A phinisi charter for five or six nights reaches anchorages that no land-based itinerary can, and it removes the daily packing entirely.

blocks.heading: Bali, chosen carefully
blocks.caption: Ridge and cliff villas away from the south.
paras: Bali is still worth it, and almost nothing in the south of the island is. The ridges above the river valleys and the eastern cliffs are a different place.
We use Bali as the arrival and the recovery, three nights either side of the boat, in houses rather than resorts.

blocks.heading: Diving and the dragons
blocks.caption: Komodo and Flores, reached by water.
paras: The water east of Bali holds some of the best diving in the world and the currents are serious.
We match the guide to the member's certification honestly, and we plan around tides rather than around a schedule.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: April to October for Bali, Komodo and Flores. Sumatra and the Moluccas run on different patterns.
For six or more people, it usually costs less per head than equivalent rooms ashore, and it reaches places they cannot.
Twelve nights minimum if a boat is involved. Shorter trips are better spent on one island.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
